Naples ’44
About Timeline Places People Folklore Themes

Theme

Crime & banditry

Camorra, bandits, vendettas, organized crime

Appears in 17 diary entries.

  1. December 5 1943
    Lewis avoids an unwanted arrest by spending the day on unrelated errands, reflecting on the unit's discomfort with being used for private vendettas.
    • Crime & banditry
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
  2. December 18 1943
    Lewis describes how gullible unit commanders and their local interpreters get dragged into baseless denunciations and village feuds, including against a corrupt police marshal.
    • Crime & banditry
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
  3. December 20 1943
    Investigating a wartime denunciation case, Lewis interviews an informer with a criminal record about his role in betraying escaped Indian soldiers to the Germans.
    • War & violence
    • Crime & banditry
  4. January 5 1944
    Lewis takes charge of security for several nearby towns, unknowingly located deep in Camorra territory, and finds poverty behind their picturesque exteriors.
    • Poverty & hunger
    • Crime & banditry
  5. January 7 1944
    A visit to Donna Maria "La Pitonessa," a former circus performer turned wealthy landowner, in the Camorra zone.
    • Crime & banditry
    • Naples's character
  6. February 5 1944
    Thieves brazenly strip the wheels from vehicles at the supposedly secure Field Security Headquarters, showcasing local audacity and ingenuity.
    • Crime & banditry
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
  7. May 3 1944
    The story of Domenico "Lupo" (Wolf), a released bandit who reorganizes his Camorra-style Robin Hood operation with Allied-issued credentials.
    • Crime & banditry
  8. May 7 (ii) 1944
    Frustrated by unresolved banditry, the General pressures Italian police into a harsher new anti-bandit operation, which Lewis observes as an onlooker.
    • Crime & banditry
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
  9. May 11 1944
    A visit to the confident, well-connected prisoner Fortuna, who expects to be acquitted of a penicillin-racketeering charge despite Lewis's evidence.
    • Black market
    • Crime & banditry
  10. June 4 1944
    A brutal act of vigilante revenge against Moroccan soldiers accused of atrocities is reported, carried out with ritualized, disturbing cruelty.
    • War & violence
    • Crime & banditry
  11. August 20 1944
    The local Marshal frets over bandit threats to the town, but Lewis notes how absurdly under-armed and unprepared the local security forces really are.
    • Crime & banditry
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
  12. August 21 1944
    A schoolmaster explains the long, entrenched history of banditry in Southern Italy, including bandits' traditional ties to landowners.
    • Crime & banditry
  13. August 25 1944
    A grenade attack on an MP sergeant prompts a tense but ultimately toothless conference about how to respond to the now-motorized bandits.
    • Crime & banditry
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
  14. September 11 1944
    A reported gangland-style shooting near a café vanishes without a trace or a single willing witness, revealing the town's undercurrent of fear and silence.
    • Crime & banditry
  15. September 16 1944
    A section colleague is shot and wounded by a bandit disguised as an American officer, forcing Lewis to weigh his own role in the anti-bandit effort.
    • War & violence
    • Crime & banditry
  16. September 19 1944
    A tense overnight checkpoint operation against suspected bandit traffic is set up on a lonely road, staffed by a poorly coordinated mix of Allied and Italian forces.
    • Crime & banditry
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
  17. September 20 1944
    A search for confiscated goods turns up little, and Lewis senses a cooling, more guarded attitude from the Marshal and townspeople toward him. He reflects that what he'd been treating as bribery may really be a customary, expected exchange of courtesy gifts — and that his own rigid refusal of it has cost him local goodwill.
    • Crime & banditry
    • Personal reflection
